Based on the provided context, Edwin Hubble's 1929 measurements of galaxy velocities and redshifts provided empirical proof that the universe is expanding. This observation directly validated the theoretical predictions of Albert Einstein, whose equations of general relativity originally indicated that the universe could not remain static but must either expand or contract. Hubble's findings convinced Einstein to abandon his long-held bias toward a static universe model.
